title: How Cursor recruits elite AI engineers when huge salaries aren't enough
excerpt: Cursor is pulling out all the stops to nab top talent. Matt Ward, the company's head of talent, said recruiting the best takes a coordinated effort.
content_html:
By Lakshmi Varanasi

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

In the fight for elite AI talent, the salary is the easy part.

At Cursor, the $60 billion company behind a suite of popular coding tools recently acquired by SpaceX, hiring a candidate is a bit like trying to win over someone who's completely out of your league.

"Closing is a team sport," Matt Ward, Cursor's head of talent, said on a recent episode of the "People by WTF" podcast. For some high-profile candidates, he said, "there are often daily standups around that candidate about what we're doing to get them to yes."

The company has also created private Slack channels dedicated to individual recruits, giving employees a place to coordinate outreach, dinners, meetings, and other parts of the courtship.

In the AI universe, where many millions of dollars in salary and perks are often not enough to recruit a top candidate, wins can come down to making a candidate feel wanted.

Ward said that after learning that one sought-after candidate had attended a performing-arts high school and trained as a classical violinist, the company tracked down a specialty music store in New York and bought him an unusual stringed instrument, which Ward described as a kind of Turkish guitar.

The gift itself wasn't especially expensive. "It's the thoughtfulness and the touch and the uniqueness of it," Ward said.

The company's CEO, Michael Truell, said on A16z's podcast last year that Cursor used "crazy recruiting stunts" to score its first 10 hires, including "flying across the world to the person after they say no."

Ward said Cursor's recruiting process has become more systematized as the company has grown.

Rather than treating recruiting as a numbers game — message a hundred people, interview whoever responds, and gradually narrow the pool — Ward said he prefers to identify the relatively small number of people who could truly excel at a job and then pursue them deliberately.

"There are 50 people in the world who can do this," he said, describing the mindset. "Let's go find those 50 people."

Then, he said, he "relentlessly" pursues them.

Cursor's approach reflects the new realities of the AI boom: For those at the top of the market, offering more money may not be enough.

The same coveted engineers can have multiple enormous offers, prestigious jobs, valuable equity, and access to cutting-edge work. Winning them over can come down to whether they connect with a company's mission and people — and whether they feel understood.

The race has changed the way major companies across Silicon Valley think about hiring, with some of the most aggressive recruiting efforts coming directly from the top.

Mark Zuckerberg has personally emailed AI researchers he wanted to bring to Meta. OpenAI chief research officer Mark Chen later said that Zuckerberg had once hand-delivered soup to an OpenAI employee Meta was trying to woo — a tactic that apparently left such an impression that OpenAI began sending soup in its own recruiting efforts.

That's not to say money doesn't matter.

Former Google HR chief Laszlo Bock has said that spending $100 million to secure a truly exceptional AI researcher could still amount to a "bargain" for a tech giant, given both what that person could build and the advantage of keeping them away from a competitor.

"You're getting NBA player-like offers and salaries, and sometimes greater than that," Ward said.

在人工智能精英人才的争夺中，薪资是最容易的部分。

Cursor 是一家价值 600 亿美元的公司，最近被 SpaceX 收购，开发了一套流行的编码工具，雇用一名候选人有点像试图赢得一个完全不在你的联盟之外的人。

“结束是一项团队运动，”Cursor 人才主管马特·沃德 (Matt Ward) 在最近一集的“People by WTF”播客中说道。 他说，对于一些备受瞩目的候选人，“每天都会围绕该候选人举行站立会议，讨论我们正在采取哪些措施让他们同意。”

该公司还创建了专门针对个人招聘的私人 Slack 频道，为员工提供了一个协调外展、晚餐、会议和求爱其他部分的地方。

在人工智能领域，数百万美元的薪水和福利往往不足以招募到顶尖候选人，胜利可以归结为让候选人感到被需要。

沃德表示，在得知一位受欢迎的候选人曾就读于表演艺术高中并接受过古典小提琴家培训后，该公司找到了纽约的一家专业音乐商店，为他购买了一种不寻常的弦乐器，沃德将其描述为一种土耳其吉他。

礼物本身并不是特别昂贵。 “这是它的体贴、触感和独特性，”沃德说。

该公司首席执行官迈克尔·特鲁尔(Michael Truell)去年在 A16z 的播客上表示，Cursor 使用“疯狂的招聘特技”来招募前 10 名员工，其中包括“在对方拒绝后飞遍世界各地去找他们”。

Ward 表示，随着公司的发展，Cursor 的招聘流程变得更加系统化。

沃德表示，他并没有将招聘视为一场数字游戏——给一百个人发消息，面试任何回应的人，并逐渐缩小范围——他更愿意找出相对少数能够真正在某项工作中表现出色的人，然后刻意追求他们。

“世界上有 50 个人可以做到这一点，”他在描述这种心态时说道。 “我们去找那五十个人吧。”

然后，他说，他“不懈地”追捕他们。

Cursor 的方法反映了人工智能繁荣的新现实：对于那些处于市场顶端的公司来说，提供更多资金可能还不够。

同样令人垂涎的工程师可以拥有多个巨大的工作机会、享有声望的工作、宝贵的股权以及接触尖端工作的机会。 赢得他们的青睐取决于他们是否与公司的使命和员工有联系，以及他们是否感到被理解。

这场竞争改变了硅谷各大公司对招聘的思考方式，一些最积极的招聘工作直接来自高层。

马克·扎克伯格亲自给人工智能研究人员发了电子邮件，他希望将其带到 Meta。 OpenAI 首席研究官马克·陈 (Mark Chen) 后来表示，扎克伯格曾经亲手给 Meta 试图吸引的 OpenAI 员工送汤——这种策略显然给人留下了这样的印象，以至于 OpenAI 开始在自己的招聘活动中送汤。

这并不是说钱不重要。

谷歌前人力资源主管拉斯洛·博克(Laszlo Bock)表示，考虑到该人可以创造什么以及让他们远离竞争对手的优势，花1亿美元聘请一位真正杰出的人工智能研究人员对于科技巨头来说仍然是一笔“划算”的交易。

“你会得到像 NBA 球员一样的报价和薪水，有时甚至更高，”沃德说。
